findings.passage: "It is critical that we uphold state authority to determine voter qualifications and ensure the integrity of our elections," said Attorney General Lynn Fitch. "Noncitizens cannot vote and should not be on the voter rolls and today the Supreme Court granted Virginia the opportunity to do what is fair and right."
findings.note: Press release from the AG's office (page: https://attorneygenerallynnfitch.com/2024/10/30/ag-fitch-praises-supreme-court-decision-allowing-virginia-to-remove-non-citizens-from-voter-rolls-october-30-2024/). She joined 25 other states' attorneys general in an amicus brief supporting Virginia's removal of self-identified noncitizens from its voter rolls.

findings.passage: "We fully support encouraging voter registration and promoting an engaged electorate," said Attorney General Lynn Fitch. "But putting the full weight of the Oval Office behind an effort first developed by partisan activist groups and then hiding the agency activities from public scrutiny goes too far. The law does not allow it. Mississippi will not stand for it. The people deserve answers, and we demand accountability here with this suit."
findings.note: Joint release with the Governor and Secretary of State announcing a state suit against Executive Order 14019 (federal agency voter registration effort). Concerns voter registration drives, not ID or citizenship proof; saved as related election material. Page: https://attorneygenerallynnfitch.com/2024/08/14/mississippi-sues-biden-administration-over-partisan-voter-registration-order-august-13-2024/
subjects: voter registration drives by federal agencies

findings.passage: Jackson has no authority to suspend open carry and it is shameful to use the current crisis as a pretext to revoke the constitutional rights of the people,
findings.note: Statement in a press release (PDF attached to the page) on filing a friend-of-the-court brief against the City of Jackson's order suspending open carry; calls open carry a fundamental right.
subjects: state law over city gun limits

findings.passage: The Constitution is clear: Law-abiding Americans have the right to protect themselves. I support the Second Amendment, and I will continue to uphold the Constitution and protect your right to bear arms.
findings.note: Quote in a press release on joining 23 state attorneys general in a Supreme Court friend-of-the-court brief in the New York carry-licence case, supporting carry outside the home.
subjects: carry a gun outside the home

findings.passage: Today’s opinion is a victory for law-abiding gun owners and for the Second Amendment.
findings.note: Official statement on the Supreme Court's Bruen decision striking New York's 'proper cause' carry-licence rule; the statement also says courts risk putting the Legislature's views above constitutionally protected rights when they balance interests.
subjects: limits on gun laws by courts

findings.passage: The right to bear arms is central to our freedom, and Congress should protect that right and repeal the provisions that the Court found to be unconstitutional. I am proud to stand with my colleagues from across the country in defense of this fundamental freedom.
findings.note: Quote in a press release on joining 20 other attorneys general in a letter asking Congress to repeal National Firearms Act provisions (suppressors) a Texas federal court held unconstitutional.
subjects: repeal National Firearms Act rules on suppressors

findings.motion: Amicus brief, Viramontes v. Cook County and Grant v. Higgins (U.S. Supreme Court), filed with 27 attorneys general against a categorical ban on AR-15 and other semi-automatic rifles
findings.note: Press release of 9 Sept 2026 says she filed the brief 'last week'; it argues the Second Amendment does not allow a categorical ban on semi-automatic rifles in common use. Filing date is approximate.

findings.motion: Joined 20-attorney-general letter to Congress urging repeal of National Firearms Act provisions on suppressors
findings.note: Signed on to a multistate letter asking Congress to repeal the NFA provisions at issue in Silencer Shop Foundation v. ATF.
subjects: repeal National Firearms Act rules on suppressors

findings.note: Joined multistate friend-of-the-court briefs supporting the challenge to New York's carry-licence 'proper cause' rule; the cert-stage brief is dated 3 Feb 2021 per the 2021 release.
